summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of gold loan default and auction processes, aligning with RBI guidelines, but some specific numerical claims regarding notice periods and reserve prices are outdated or slightly inaccurate based on the latest regulations.

claims.claim: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has laid down specific guidelines that lenders, including banks and Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), must adhere to when dealing with gold loan defaults. Under its Master Circular on Fair Practices Code for Lenders, specific guidelines apply to gold loans, particularly concerning valuation, loan-to-value (LTV) ratios, and recovery procedures.
claims.note: The RBI Master Circular on Fair Practices Code for Lenders (July 1, 2015) covers general principles for NBFCs, including aspects of loan appraisal, terms/conditions, and recovery methods. More recent directions specifically for gold loans also exist.

claims.claim: When you take a gold loan, the gold jewellery is valued by an approved appraiser, and the loan amount is disbursed based on a Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio, which is typically capped at 75% for non-agricultural gold loans by banks.
claims.note: As of April 1, 2026, RBI guidelines for consumption gold loans have a tiered LTV structure: up to 85% for loans up to ₹2.5 lakh, 80% for loans between ₹2.5 lakh and ₹5 lakh, and 75% for loans above ₹5 lakh.

claims.claim: As per RBI guidelines, lenders must provide a reasonable notice period to the borrower before proceeding with the auction of the pledged gold. This period is generally 30 days from the date of the final notice.
claims.note: RBI guidelines mandate a minimum notice period ranging from 10 to 21 days, or 15-30 days, depending on the lender's policy, before the auction. Some sources mention 14 days.

claims.claim: The auction must be advertised in at least two newspapers, one in the local language and one in a national daily, well in advance of the auction date.
claims.note: RBI guidelines state that the auction must be announced to the public by advertisements in at least two newspapers, one in the regional language and another in a national daily.

claims.claim: A minimum reserve price for the auction is then set, which should not be less than 80% of the current market value of the gold.
claims.note: As per RBI guidelines, the reserve price for the gold collateral at the time of auction shall not be less than 90% of its current value. If two auctions fail, a reserve price not less than 85% can be adopted. Some sources mention 85% of the average closing price of 22-carat gold over the last 30 working days.

claims.claim: If there is any surplus amount after recovering all dues, the lender is obligated to return this surplus to the borrower.
claims.note: After the auction, any surplus from the auction proceeds must be refunded to the borrower.

claims.claim: If the auction proceeds are less than the outstanding dues, the borrower may still be liable to pay the remaining deficit.
claims.note: The lender may recover any shortfall as per the terms of the loan agreement.

article_title: Gold Loan EMI Default: When Your Pledged Jewellery is at Risk
